mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals a weakening demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining RSAFS, or the correlation between RSAFS declines and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals an inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending improve.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last three months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity and related sectors benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of periods with increasing HOUST, or the correlation between HOUST increases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters, it signals a recessionary environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic activity decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of recessionary periods, or the correlation between negative GDPC1 growth and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
